question: Does repeated prior strong-chorus use of the same physical SiteID by a species dose-dependently predict where that route-new species reactivates in a wetter survey?
population: Physically stable matched pairs with prior eligible history in the same State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum. Focal species are absent from the focal dry route, present in the wet route, and previously recorded somewhere on the route.
unit: pair x focal species x physical SiteID with at least two prior sampling opportunities for that SiteID

predictors.own_prior_strong_rate: Fraction of prior eligible opportunities at that SiteID with focal-species CallingIndex 2-3.
predictors.generic_other_strong_rate: Across the same prior opportunities, mean number of other species with CallingIndex 2-3 at the SiteID.
predictors.own_prior_any_rate: Fraction of prior opportunities with any focal-species CallingIndex >0; alternate sensitivity only.

outcomes.wet_strong: 1 if focal species has wet CallingIndex 2-3.
outcomes.wet_full: 1 if focal species has wet CallingIndex 3.

primary_design: Restrict to pair x species groups with within-group variation in own_prior_strong_rate. Demean wet_strong, own_prior_strong_rate and generic_other_strong_rate within pair x species; regress demeaned wet_strong on the two predictors without intercept; cluster covariance by State x RouteNumber.
primary_prediction: own_prior_strong_rate coefficient >0 with complete 95% CI >0 after generic site chorus quality is controlled.
secondary: Replace own_prior_strong_rate with own_prior_any_rate while retaining generic-other-strong control.
minimum_gate: At least 400 informative pair x species groups, >=225 routes and >=20 species after requiring at least two prior SiteID opportunities.
interpretation: A positive dose response supports durable species-site recurrence beyond a one-off historical detection and generic frog-hotspot quality.
It remains compatible with persistent local populations and species-specific microhabitat suitability; these are not distinguished.
No continuous occupancy, individual identity, reproductive success or causal rainfall claim.
